Quotations name only their work and their words: scripts/theory-pages.mjs places them in the read-only corpus and writes the locator from the corpus's own markers; one it cannot place exactly once fails the build. Where the scan itself is damaged inside the sentence (letters-pauli p160), the quotation is kept as the scan reads it and says so (`scan`), never repaired by hand.
line: Where Jung uses the word and what he says it names: in the essays of 1946–1954, in the synchronicity essay, and in his letters with the physicist Wolfgang Pauli.

sections.title: The naming
sections.line: The synchronicity essay (CW8 ¶840, 1952) says what Jung has named psychoid and why.

quotes.quote: The latter represents a psyche that is identical in all individuals.
It cannot be directly perceived or "represented," in contrast to the perceptible psychic phenomena, and on account of its "irrepresentable" nature I have called it "psychoid."

sections.title: The three reservations
sections.line: On the Nature of the Psyche (CW8 ¶368): the three reservations on his use of the word, and Bleuler as its source.

quotes.quote: I do so with three reservations: firstly, I use it as an adjective, not as a noun; secondly, no psychic quality in the proper sense of the word is implied, but only a "quasi-psychic" one such as the reflex-processes possess; and thirdly, it is meant to distinguish a category of events from merely vitalistic phenomena on the one hand and from specifically psychic processes on the other.
although it is always the function that creates its own organ, and maintains or modifies it.
although my use of the term derives from a different field of perception, it nevertheless seeks to delineate roughly the same group of phenomena that Bleuler had in mind.

sections.title: The form under the image
sections.line: The Spirit Mercurius (CW13 ¶350): the psychoid form underlying an archetypal image.

quotes.quote: The psychoid form underlying any archetypal image retains its character at all stages of development, though empirically it is capable of endless variations.

sections.title: The ultra-violet end
sections.line: On the Nature of the Psyche (CW8 ¶417): the archetype as such is placed at the ultra-violet end of the psychic spectrum.

quotes.quote: The archetypal representations (images and ideas) mediated to us by the unconscious should not be confused with the archetype as such. They are very varied structures which all point back to one essentially "irrepresentable" basic form.
The latter is characterized by certain formal elements and by certain fundamental meanings, although these can be grasped only approximately.
The archetype as such is a psychoid factor that belongs, as it were, to the invisible, ultraviolet end of the psychic spectrum.

Since other archetypes give rise to similar doubts, it seems to me probable that the real nature of the archetype is not capable of being made conscious, that it is transcendent, on which account I call it psychoid.

sections.title: The physics parallel
sections.line: CW8 ¶419–420: the psychic spectrum set beside the physicist's irrepresentable models, and what Jung says follows for psyche and matter.

quotes.quote: When the existence of two or more irrepresentables is assumed, there is always the possibility—which we tend to overlook—that it may not be a question of two or more factors but of one only.
The identity or non-identity of two irrepresentable quantities is something that cannot be proved.

Since psyche and matter are contained in one and the same world, and moreover are in continuous contact with one another and ultimately rest on irrepresentable, transcendental factors, it is not only possible but fairly probable, even, that psyche and matter are two different aspects of one and the same thing.

Just as the "psychic infra-red," the biological instinctual psyche, gradually passes over into the physiology of the organism and thus merges with its chemical and physical conditions, so the "psychic ultra-violet," the archetype, describes a field which exhibits none of the peculiarities of the physiological and yet, in the last analysis, can no longer be regarded as psychic, although it manifests itself psychically.
Although there is no form of existence that is not mediated to us psychically and only psychically, it would hardly do to say that everything is merely psychic.
the psyche and its contents are the only reality which is given to us ioithout a medium.

sections.title: The specific charge
sections.line: CW8 ¶841, the paragraph after the naming: what the archetypes are said to be and to do.

quotes.quote: The archetypes are formal factors responsible for the organization of unconscious psychic processes: they are "patterns of behaviour."
At the same time they have a "specific charge" and develop numinous effects which express themselves as affects.

sections.title: Not localized in one person
sections.line: Flying Saucers: A Modern Myth (CW10 ¶851): how the psychoid archetype is said to behave.

quotes.quote: The psychoid archetype has a tendency to behave as though it were not localized in one person but were active in the whole environment.

sections.title: In Jung's letters to Pauli
sections.line: Atom and Archetype, the Pauli–Jung letters: Jung's statements of 1951 and 1953 on the archetype's physical and psychic occurrence.

quotes.quote: With the merely psychoid (transcendental) nature of the archetype, its purely physical occurrence is by no means precluded.
it is based on the psychoid archetype, which, as experience has shown, can be express itseII both psychically and physically.
The characteristic that is peculiar to the archetype is that it manifests itself not only psychically-subjectively but also physically-objectively

sections.title: Whole numbers
sections.line: Letter 63 (October 1953): Jung on whole numbers and the psychoid archetype.

quotes.quote: that they are as much inside as outside. Thus, one can never make out whether they have been devised or discovered; as numbers they are inside and as a quantity they are outside.

sections.title: Pauli's side
sections.line: Pauli's own words: the objection of December 1950, and a letter of December 1953 (66P).

quotes.quote: but also the concept of the (psychic or psychoid) archetype cannot be used so lightly in the acausalities of microphysics.
what is happening is ultimately an assimilation of the psychoid archetypes into an extended form of physics.

sections.title: The late admission
sections.line: CW8 ¶599, a note added in 1948 to 'The Psychological Foundations of Belief in Spirits'.

quotes.quote: Not only the findings of parapsychology, but my own theoretical reflections, outlined in "On the Nature of the Psyche," have led me to certain postulates which touch on the realm of nuclear physics and the conception of the space-time continuum. This opens up the whole question of the transpsychic reality immediately underlying the psyche.

sections.title: The last word
sections.line: CW18 ¶1208, a letter to Michael Fordham (1955): the term in its late form.

quotes.quote: Synchronicity tells us something about the nature of what I call the psychoid factor, i.e., the unconscious archetype (not its conscious representation!).
